description: Tall, strongly fragrant cut flower stock with 32" stems and very early, programmable timing (7–11 weeks in fall, 8–13 weeks in spring). Uniform stem length across the mix. Approximately 50% double flowering, which is normal for stock. Best suited for cool greenhouse, tunnel, or open field.
sowingNotes: Sow November in pots or trays under cool cover (45–55°F). Can also be sown January–February as an insurance sowing using the same seed. Grows best in cool, bright conditions — cold frame or unheated greenhouse, not a warm house.

description: Classic 30" cut flower snapdragon, fragrant, with strong upright spikes suited for field or greenhouse production. The Rocket series is a standard professional cut flower choice. Available in individual colours (Bronze, Golden Yellow, Orchid, Pink, Red, White) and mix.
sowingNotes: Sow November in pots or trays under cool cover (45–55°F). Also sow January–February for a second wave. Needs cool, bright conditions to develop strong stems.

description: Tall double azalea-flowered snapdragon, 30", described as a superb cut flower. F1 hybrid for uniform timing and stem quality. AAS award winner. Available in individual colours (Bronze, Ivory, Pink, Red, Yellow) and mix.
sowingNotes: Sow November in pots or trays under cool cover (45–55°F). Also suitable for a January–February insurance sowing.

description: Group IV tall snapdragon (32–40") with solid spikes on sturdy stems. Named replacement for the discontinued Costa Summer series in the GeoSeed catalog. Well suited to greenhouse, tunnel, or open ground production.
sowingNotes: Sow November in pots or trays under cool cover (45–55°F). Also suitable for January–February insurance sowing.

description: Giant Imperial type larkspur at 32", a reliable direct-sown cut flower. The Imperial Choice Mix is an exact match for traditional cut flower larkspur plantings. Direct sow only — taproot resents transplanting. Suited to the back of the border.
sowingNotes: Direct sow outdoors in November into a raised, well-drained bed. Cold stratification happens naturally over winter. Most fall sowing failures are caused by poor drainage, not cold. Do not transplant.

description: Extra-select double bicolour cornflower mix suited to field-grown cut flower, borders, and mass landscape plantings. Direct sown. The Frosty Mix includes frosted bicolour tones not found in standard bachelor's button mixes.
sowingNotes: Direct sow outdoors in November into a raised, well-drained bed. Hardy annual that benefits from cold conditioning over winter.

description: Traditional double-flowered Love-in-a-Mist, direct sown to field. Both the intricate blue-green flowers and the striped, inflated seed pods are useful in arrangements. Available in single colours (Indigo, Light Blue, White) and mix.
sowingNotes: Direct sow outdoors in November. Taproot — does not transplant well. Scatter seed in a prepared bed.

description: 24" long-stemmed calendula with double and semi-double flowers in orange, apricot, cream, and lemon tones. A classic direct-sown cut flower. Available in single colours (Apricot, Cream, Lemon, Orange w/ Brown Eye) and mix.
sowingNotes: Direct sow outdoors in November into a well-drained bed. Can also be sown in early spring. Cold-hardy and tolerant of light frost.

description: 6-foot fragrant climbing sweet pea bred specifically for cut flower production under short days — the best fit for a November sowing aimed at late April to May flowering. Available in single colours (Burgundy, Deep Rose, Mid Blue, White) and mix. Note: a Bed 3 fence row will require multiple packs as each pack is only 100 seeds.
sowingNotes: Sow November in deep root-trainers under cool cover (45–55°F). Pre-chill seed 4 weeks at 32–35°F, then soak overnight before sowing 1" deep. Needs a trellis or fence. Quantity note: 100 seeds per Trade Pkt — plan on multiple packs for a full fence row.

description: Bulk sweet pea mix available in true bulk bags from Everwilde Farms. Approximately 300 seeds per ounce. Priced competitively at ~$19–20 per 1,000 seeds at the 1 lb size. A practical choice for large-scale plantings where a named Spencer variety is not required.
sowingNotes: Sow in deep root-trainers under cool cover. Pre-soak overnight. Needs a trellis or fence. Climbs to 6 feet.

description: F1 hybrid Iceland poppy, 15", with uniform timing, sturdy stems, and large flowers. Primed seed for reliable germination. Available in single colours (Orange, Pink, Scarlet, White, Yellow) and mix. GeoSeed's primary Iceland poppy series. Note: Colibri types from Biancheri/Onings America are a separate, PBR-protected commercial variety — Champagne Bubbles is GeoSeed's listed series.
sowingNotes: Sow November in individual pots — Iceland poppies strongly resent root disturbance. Keep cool and bright (cold frame or unheated greenhouse). Do not transplant bareroot.

description: 2-foot double Shirley-type poppy mix in cherry, cream, orange, lilac, and mauve bicolour tones. A fresh local cut flower classic, field sown. The American Legion (red Flanders type) is a separate variety — Angel's Choir is the Shirley mix.
sowingNotes: Direct sow outdoors in November into a well-drained bed. Scatter seed on the surface; poppies need light to germinate. Do not bury seed deeply.

description: Low-growing front-of-border filler with fragrant small flowers. Not carried by GeoSeed or Johnny's — Everwilde Farms is the verified source. Available in bulk sizes up to 50 lb.
sowingNotes: Direct sow. Suited to front-of-border or low edging. Can be scattered in gaps between taller plants.

description: Classic ornamental and culinary poppy with large, showy flowers and ornamental seedpods useful in dried arrangements. Not carried by GeoSeed or Johnny's. Reimer Seeds is the verified source, offering 1,000-seed packs and bulk sizes up to 1 lb. Germination rate on file: 85%.
sowingNotes: Direct sow late fall for natural cold stratification. 1,266,000 seeds per pound. Scatter on the soil surface; needs light to germinate.
